---
name: paid-social
description: Build a Facebook/Instagram campaign that drives qualified WhatsApp conversations or landing-page actions, with five creatives, one video, a message flow, and a measurement model. Use for digital products and local offers.
version: 1.0.0
license: MIT
allowed-tools: Read, Write
---

# Paid Social

## When to use

Use when the user has a clear offer, a real audience, and a destination (WhatsApp or landing page). Do not use it to “boost” a post with no offer.

## Inputs

| Variable | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{{offer}}` | yes | What is sold, price, discount, guarantee |
| `{{audience}}` | yes | Country, age, interests, exclusions |
| `{{proof}}` | yes | Reviews, delivery proof, customer video |
| `{{destination}}` | yes | WhatsApp number or landing page |
| `{{budget}}` | yes | Daily budget and test window |

## Process

1. Choose the objective: WhatsApp conversations, leads, or sales.
2. Define the audience: broad, interest, lookalike, retargeting.
3. Write the offer in one sentence, with the delivery and validity terms.
4. Create five image concepts + one video concept.
5. Write three hooks per concept, two CTAs.
6. Build the WhatsApp/landing flow: greeting, qualify, quote, proof, close, deliver, follow-up.
7. Define the metrics: cost per conversation, qualified rate, close rate, AOV, ROAS, refund rate.
8. Set the weekly optimisation cadence.

## Output

- `campaign.md` — objective, audience, budget, placements, bidding.
- `creatives.md` — five image prompts + one video brief.
- `copy.md` — headlines, primary text, descriptions, CTAs.
- `flow.md` — WhatsApp/landing script.
- `measurement.md` — KPIs and review cadence.

## Compliance

- Only advertise products you are authorised to sell.
- State region, platform, delivery time, and validity.
- Do not use “official” or a publisher’s logo to imply endorsement.
- No fake countdowns, fake “only 2 left,” or fake reviews.
- WhatsApp opt-in must be explicit; no purchased lists.
- Honour the replacement/refund policy you advertise.

## QA

- [ ] Offer is true and deliverable.
- [ ] Audience and region defined.
- [ ] Five creatives + one video.
- [ ] No fake scarcity or discounts.
- [ ] WhatsApp opt-in explicit.
- [ ] Flow matches the ad.
- [ ] Delivery time and validity stated.
- [ ] Cost per conversation tracked.
- [ ] Weekly optimisation scheduled.

## References

- `prompts/09-paid-social.md`
- `playbooks/paid-social.md`
- `checklists/paid-social-qa.md`
- `templates/campaign-brief.md`

<!-- ===== skills\product-listing\SKILL.md ===== -->

---
name: product-listing
description: Build a digital product listing that answers what it is, who it is for, what you get, how it arrives, how long it lasts, and why it is safe to buy. Use for software keys, subscriptions, templates, and digital goods.
version: 1.0.0
license: MIT
allowed-tools: Read, Write
---

# Product Listing

## When to use

Use when the user wants a product page, marketplace listing, or listing refresh for a digital product.

## Inputs

| Variable | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{{product}}` | yes | Product name and what it does |
| `{{product_url}}` | yes | The canonical listing URL |
| `{{facts}}` | yes | Licence, delivery, validity, region, support |
| `{{competitors}}` | yes | 3–5 real alternatives |
| `{{proof}}` | yes | Screenshots, reviews, delivery proof |
| `{{images}}` | no | Existing assets; otherwise generate prompts |

## Process

1. Write the title: 60–70 characters, product + differentiator + audience.
2. Choose one focus keyphrase and 2–3 secondary.
3. Write the short description: 150–160 characters.
4. Write the long description: 800–1,500 words.
5. Build the comparison table with verified criteria.
6. Write 5–7 FAQs: delivery, validity, compatibility, refund, support.
7. Specify delivery time, validity, region, device limit.
8. Write the meta description, slug, category, and 5–7 tags.
9. Create the five-image set with prompt, ALT, title, description, ratio, placement.
10. Run the QA gate.

## Output

- `listing.md` — title, descriptions, comparison, FAQ, delivery, validity, meta, slug, tags.
- `images.md` — five prompts + metadata.
- `qa.md` — compliance and accuracy checks.

## Trust layer

Every listing must answer:

- What exactly do I get?
- How is it delivered?
- How long does it last?
- Will it work in my region?
- What if it fails?
- Are you authorised to sell it?

## Compliance

- Do not claim “official,” “authorised,” or “genuine” without proof.
- Do not sell accounts or keys in violation of the vendor’s terms.
- Do not use “lifetime” when you mean “until the vendor changes the plan.”
- Do not use fake discounts, reviews, or scarcity.
- Do not imply endorsement with another company’s trademark.

## QA

- [ ] Title 60–70 characters.
- [ ] Focus keyphrase in title, H1, first 100 words, meta.
- [ ] Short description 150–160 characters.
- [ ] Long description answers what/who/how/how long.
- [ ] Comparison table uses verified data.
- [ ] FAQ covers delivery, validity, compatibility, refund, support.
- [ ] Product schema matches visible facts.
- [ ] Five images with alt text.
- [ ] No fake reviews, discounts, or “official” claims.
- [ ] Support and policy pages linked.

## References

- `prompts/07-listing.md`
- `playbooks/listing-engine.md`
- `checklists/listing-qa.md`
- `templates/listing.md`

---
name: repurposer

version: 1.0.0
license: MIT
allowed-tools: Read, Write
---

# Repurposer

## When to use

Use after an article, listing, or report is published. Do not use it to cross-post the same paragraph everywhere.

## Inputs

| Variable | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{{canonical}}` | yes | The published article or asset |
| `{{platforms}}` | yes | 3–4 platforms chosen by buyer fit |
| `{{cta}}` | yes | The one action per platform |
| `{{proof}}` | yes | The strongest number, quote, or visual |

## Platform fit

| Business | Core | Secondary | Skip |
|---|---|---|---|
| B2B SaaS | LinkedIn, X, Medium, YouTube | Reddit, newsletter | Pinterest, Tumblr |
| Local service | Facebook, Instagram, GBP, YouTube | WhatsApp status, local groups | X, Threads |
| E-commerce / digital goods | Instagram, Pinterest, YouTube, Facebook | X, Threads, Telegram | LinkedIn (unless B2B) |
| Agency / consultant | LinkedIn, YouTube, newsletter, X | Medium, podcast | Pinterest |

## Process

1. Choose 3–4 platforms. Explain why.
2. For each, write a native post: different hook, same facts.
3. Add one image prompt per visual platform, with ALT, title, description, ratio, placement.
4. Add the CTA that fits the platform.
5. Return a publishing calendar for the week.

## Output

```markdown
| Platform | Format | Hook | CTA | Metric | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
```

Plus the post copy, image prompts, and a 5-day calendar.

## Rules

- Derivatives may change the hook, format, and length.
- They may not change the facts, price, links, or claim.
- One idea per post.
- No platform is used just because it exists.
- No fake urgency or engagement bait.

## QA

- [ ] Each post has a different hook.
- [ ] Facts, price, and links match the canonical asset.
- [ ] Format is native to the platform.
- [ ] CTA fits the platform’s behaviour.
- [ ] Image has alt text and a reason to exist.
- [ ] Post can stand alone.
- [ ] One metric per platform.

## References

- `prompts/06-repurpose.md`
- `playbooks/content-factory.md`

---
name: seo-orchestrator
description: Routes an SEO request to the right skill and pipeline, runs the three-question intake, checks tool connections, and enforces the two checkpoints. Use when the user asks for SEO help without naming a specific skill.

# SEO Orchestrator

## When to use

Use this skill when the request is broad — “help me with SEO,” “audit my site,” “grow my traffic,” “write me a content plan,” “what should I do next?” — or when the user has not named a specific pipeline.

## What you do

1. Read `kit.json` and confirm the capability list.
2. Ask the three intake questions. Stop.
3. After the answers, choose **one** pipeline:
   - Content → `skills/content-factory/SKILL.md`
   - Silo → `skills/silo-builder/SKILL.md`
   - Repurpose → `skills/repurposer/SKILL.md`
   - Listing → `skills/product-listing/SKILL.md`
   - Directory → `skills/directory-submission/SKILL.md`
   - Paid → `skills/paid-social/SKILL.md`
   - AI visibility → `skills/ai-visibility/SKILL.md`
   - Audit → `skills/technical-audit/SKILL.md`
   - Local → `skills/local-seo/SKILL.md`
4. State the pipeline, the canonical asset, the two checkpoints, and the tools you will use.
5. Run only that pipeline. Do not run three pipelines in one response.

## Intake

Ask exactly:

1. **Site** — domain or product URL.
2. **Outcome** — traffic, citations, listings, conversations, or revenue.
3. **Tools** — Ubersuggest MCP, AnswerThePublic, SpyFu, Mangools, GSC, GA4, or manual/CSV.

If the user says “I don't know,” propose one default based on the site type and ask them to confirm.

## Tool check

Read `mcp/tool-matrix.md`. For each tool:

- **MCP connected** → use it.
- **API key present** → use the API via a script or the operator's client.
- **Nothing** → ask for a CSV or say you will proceed without it. Never invent the data.

Never ask for a password, API key, or cookie in chat.

## Output

```text
Pipeline: <name>
Canonical asset: <article / listing / batch / campaign / report>
Checkpoint 1: brief/plan for approval
Checkpoint 2: publish/submit for approval
Tools: <connected> / <missing>
First action: <one sentence>
```

## Rules

- One pipeline per response.
- Cite or cut.
- No invented experience.
- No keyword density.
- One product link.
- Two checkpoints.
- If the request violates the rules, say so and offer the compliant alternative.

## References

- `AGENTS.md`
- `kit.json`
- `mcp/tool-matrix.md`
- `docs/00-start-here.md`

<!-- ===== skills\silo-builder\SKILL.md ===== -->

---
name: silo-builder
description: Build a five-silo content cluster from a money page and the questions a buyer asks before converting. Use for content plans, topical maps, cluster architecture, and internal-link planning.
version: 1.0.0
license: MIT
allowed-tools: Read, Write
---

# Silo Builder

## When to use

Use when the user asks for a content plan, topic cluster, silo, content map, or “what should we write?” Do not use it to write the pages; use `content-factory` for that.

## Inputs

| Variable | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{{keyword}}` | yes | The primary query, not a keyword list |
| `{{product_url}}` | yes | The one page that converts |
| `{{brand}}` | yes | Business name and one-line description |
| `{{market}}` | yes | Country, language, currency |
| `{{buyer}}` | yes | Role, objection, what they already tried |
| `{{proof_assets}}` | yes | Data, cases, reviews, screenshots |
| `{{internal_links}}` | yes | Pages that already exist and can be linked |
| `{{competitors}}` | no | Competitors you can name fairly |

## Process

1. Classify the primary intent: informational, commercial, transactional, navigational, local.
2. Propose **five silos**: Problem, Solution, Comparison, Use case, Proof.
3. For each silo, give **3–5 subtopics**. One page, one intent. Merge duplicates.
4. For each subtopic, specify:
   - 2–3 long-tail keywords (no invented volume)
   - the internal link target and anchor
   - 2–3 primary external sources
   - the proof asset required
   - the CTA
5. Output the table, then an ASCII map, then a scorecard.
6. Score demand, proof, winnability, conversion (1–5). If any is below 3, say what is missing.

## Output

```markdown
| Silo | Subtopic / H1 | Intent | Long-tail keywords | Internal links | External sources | Proof asset | CTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

```text
<ASCII map>
```

| Dimension | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Demand | /5 | |
| Proof | /5 | |
| Winnability | /5 | |
| Conversion | /5 | |
```

## Rules

- Do not invent search volume, difficulty, traffic, or competitor data.
- Do not create a page for a query the product cannot answer.
- One page, one intent. No cannibalisation.
- Prefer 20 strong pages over 100 thin ones.
- Mark every claim that needs verification with `[VERIFY]`.

## QA

- [ ] Five silos, each a different question.
- [ ] Every subtopic has one intent and one proof asset.
- [ ] Every money page is reachable in three clicks.
- [ ] No two subtopics target the same query.
- [ ] The scorecard is honest; anything below 3 is called out.
- [ ] No invented numbers or competitor claims.

## References

- `prompts/02-silo.md`
- `playbooks/content-factory.md`
- `examples/01-rocketclips-silo.md`

<!-- ===== skills\technical-audit\SKILL.md ===== -->

---
name: technical-audit
description: Run a 120-point audit across crawl/index, rendering/speed, on-page, content/E-E-A-T, architecture, schema, AI search, local, links, and measurement. Use for site audits and pre-launch checks.

# Technical Audit

## When to use

Use when the user asks for a site audit, technical SEO review, pre-launch check, or “why isn’t this page ranking?”

## Process

1. Run `python scripts/audit_url.py <url>` for the surface check.
2. Run `python scripts/sitemap_check.py <url>` for sitemap and status.
3. Open the 120-point checklist: `checklists/technical-audit-120.md`.
4. Score each item pass/fail. Do not average across categories.
5. Identify the top three constraints by impact.
6. Return a fix list: symptom, cause, fix, owner, effort, expected effect.

## Output

- `audit.md` — score, findings, fix list.
- `audit.json` — machine-readable findings.
- `screenshots/` — before evidence where relevant.

## Priority rules

1. Indexability of money pages.
2. Server response time and rendering.
3. Canonicals, duplicates, soft 404s.
4. Internal links to money pages.
5. Content proof and intent match.
6. Schema and entity clarity.
7. Links and local signals.

## QA

- [ ] Money pages indexed.
- [ ] robots.txt and sitemap valid.
- [ ] No accidental noindex or cross-canonical.
- [ ] Primary content in server HTML.
- [ ] LCP/INP/CLS at p75.
- [ ] Internal links to money pages.
- [ ] Schema matches visible facts.
- [ ] No manual actions.
- [ ] Fix list has owners and effort.
- [ ] Evidence captured.

## References

- `checklists/technical-audit-120.md`
- `prompts/10-qa.md`
- `scripts/audit_url.py`
- `scripts/sitemap_check.py`
